answer.rationale: The two declining metrics (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) are causally linked, with onboarding upstream of activation, so the highest-leverage single slot is the funnel step that feeds the other. memory_86 and memory_31 both point at onboarding/signup friction as a lever with durable effect, and memory_91 suggests activation messaging is a complement rather than a root-cause fix. I am deliberately NOT choosing promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing: memory_73 is the memory whose headline numbers (+31% conversions, +18% revenue) most exceed what its stated design can support — a 12-week window on a low-touch segment, with the oddly specific note that the support model was unchanged, which reads like a scope caveat that got flattened during consolidation. Discounting into a price war also risks importing exactly the price-sensitive accounts that erode long-term qualified revenue, which is the stated objective. So I spend verification on memory_73 (to see whether the promo record was ever measured against retention/revenue quality, or whether the lift was a pull-forward within a short window) and memory_86 (because my intended action rests on it, and its summary reports completion and time-to-value, not qualified revenue — I need to know whether revenue was ever measured or merely assumed downstream). Explicit downstream risk on my own choice: the mechanism in memory_31 was cutting required signup fields, which can raise activation counts while degrading lead qualification data and therefore sales-stage quality; a completion-rate win is not the same as a qualified-revenue win. So I scope this as a standard experiment with holdout, instrumented on downstream qualified pipeline and 8-12 week retention rather than completion rate alone, not a broad rollout. If the memory_73 record shows retention/quality was genuinely tracked and clean, promotional_pricing becomes a live contender for the next slot; if the memory_86 record shows no revenue-side measurement, I hold scale down to a small guarded test rather than treating the inherited lift as established.
